shared_elements: upright stone slab/pillar carved in low relief
row of repeated rectangular/boxed motifs across the upper zone
horizontal band of repeated pattern (zigzag/net or belt) crossing the surface
sinuous curved forms resembling snakes or elongated bodies
animal or creature shown in profile
vertical arm-like or pendant elements descending at the sides
suggestion of an anthropomorphic body (shoulders, torso, belt)
justification: Both are upright relief-carved stone slabs organised in the same top-down sequence: a row of repeated boxed/rectangular units at the head end, then a horizontal patterned band across the width, then discs, sinuous forms and profile creatures on the torso below, with pendant arm-like verticals at the edges. The biggest difference is the manner of rendering — A is deeply cut, dark, curvilinear and highly schematic with dominant discs and coiling lines, while B is shallow, light-toned and includes recognisably naturalistic quadrupeds and long-necked birds, so the two read as different hands and possibly different traditions despite the comparable layout.
